note: Relationships the DOCUMENT SET asserts across pages, which no single page can check. A parser can read two pages each perfectly self-consistently and still contradict itself between them -- read the fund as 1,690,818,394 on one page and 1,690,818,894 on the other and both pages still balance internally. Only an identity between them fails. Every term must come from the same parser, so this grades one tool's coherence over a document set rather than agreement between tools.

identities.name: fund_ties_to_balance_sheet
identities.why: Exhibit 2 closes at the deposit insurance fund; Exhibit 1 carries the same figure as the balancing item. The two exhibits reference each other by name on the page -- 'note 2 and exhibit 1', 'note 2 and exhibit 2'.

identities.name: assessment_credit_prior_years
identities.why: Note 1 of the income statement states the credit due the banks for prior years; the balance sheet carries it as a liability line.

identities.name: assessment_credit_estimated
identities.why: Note 1's estimated credit for the first six months of 1956 is the balance sheet's second assessment-credit line.
identities.equals: fdic_balance.ment income for 6 months ended June 30, 1956.detail

identities.name: assessment_credits_total_across_pages
identities.why: A cross-page SUM rather than an identity: the income statement's two note-1 figures add to the balance sheet's combined assessment-credit total. One term is in prose on one page, the other two in a column on the other.
identities.equals: fdic_balance.ment income for 6 months ended June 30, 1956.total

identities.name: securities_face_value
identities.why: Note 4 quotes the face value of securities held; the balance sheet prints the same figure inside the label prose of the securities line. Both are figures embedded in sentences rather than in columns, on different pages.

identities.name: cash_balance
identities.why: Note 4's cash balance is the balance sheet's first asset line.

identities.name: estimated_losses_on_open_cases
identities.why: Note 2's estimated losses on cases not terminated is the balance sheet's deduction from receivership assets.
